full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman J : This appeal by the father of a minor girl, Dhalu Rani Nandi is against the judgment and order passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division on 7-12-95 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.2332 of 1995 arising out of an application under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, regarding the custody of the said minor girl who is detained in District Jail, Tangail in connection which GR Case No.1150 (2)/94 under section 366A of the Penal Code read with section 4(6) of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983. 

 4. Police after investigation submitted charge-sheet on 20-6-95 against the accused. Md. Abdul Awal Khan, under section 366A of the Penal Code read with section 4(b) of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983. The case was transmitted to the Special Tribunal (Session Judge, Tangail) and the appellant filed an application praying for the custody of the victim girl but the Special Tribunal rejected the prayer by order dated 23-7-95. The appellant alleged that the report of the Medical Board was cancelled on the asking of the accused party and another examination was ordered by a different Medical Board without any conceivable reason. The appellant ultimately moved the High Court Division under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and a Rule was issued in Criminal Misc. Case No. 2332 of 1995. 

 5. The learned Judges after hearing the parties and upon considering the materials on record took the view that the victim girl was a minor but considering the safety and security of the girl as she had embraced Islam and married a Muslim boy it was held that ends of justice will be met if the victim girl was kept in judicial custody. The Rule was disposed of with the direction that, "Hence it is ordered that if the victim girl is willing to go with her father, she may be allowed to go with her father. But if she does not want to go with her father then she will be kept in judicial custody till the disposal of the criminal case as well as till she attains majority that is, the age of 18 years." 

 8. The learned Judges of the High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record found the victim girl, Dhalu Rani Nandi to be a minor. It is not disputed before us that under the law the father is the lawful guardian of his minor daughter. The learned Judges having found the victim girl to be a minor ought to have given the minor in the lawful custody of the father. The opinion of the minor is irrelevant and the same cannot be a condition precedent for giving her custody to the father. The learned Judges failed to consider that a minor's refusal to go with her father is not at all a material consideration regarding her custody. Father being the best well-wisher of a minor daughter is entitled to custody and in her own interest she should be given in her father's custody. Further, the minor girl is an unfortunate victim of an offence of an abduction and it is not understood why she should be detained till the disposal of the criminal case as well as till she attains the age of 18 years. It is not desirable that she should be kept in jail for a long indefinite period which will be detrimental to her welfare. In that view of the matter, the learned Judges of the High Court Division ought to have given the custody of the minor girl to the appellant. 

 9. In the present case the father is trying to get the custody of his minor daughter from the court of Magistrate up to this Division. Surely, it is prompted by filial love, affection and welfare of the minor daughter.
